title: The pro-etale field site as profinite Galois sets
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $k^s/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and let $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with the Krull topology (stabilizers of finite subextensions form an open neighborhood basis of $1$). Use small representatives and a coefficient universe containing them [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B_s$ be the full subcategory of quasi-compact quasi-separated objects of the small pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathbf{Prof}_G$ be the category of compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces with continuous left $G$-action and continuous equivariant maps. Give it coverings the families having a finite jointly surjective subfamily.

There is an equivalence $\mathcal B_s\simeq\mathbf{Prof}_G$, carrying the induced pro-etale topology to this topology. The inclusion $\mathcal B_s\subset s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is a dense subsite: every object has a covering by objects of $\mathcal B_s$, and its topology is the induced topology. Base change along $\bar s\to s$ corresponds to forgetting the $G$-action under the analogous equivalence $\mathcal B_{\bar s}\simeq\mathbf{Prof}$. For a profinite set $P$, write $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ for the test scheme of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Under the equivalence, $s[P]$ corresponds to $P$ with trivial action, while $\bar s[P]$, considered over $s$, corresponds to $G\times P$ with $G$ acting by left translation on the first factor. The identifications are natural in $P$ and take the morphism $\bar s[P]\to s[P]$ to $G\times P\to P$.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9 and 4.1.10, pp. 27-28: profinite tensor objects, qcqs objects over a field, induced covering families; density also uses affine open coverings.

proof.text: Apply the affine reduction and fibre construction to every $U\in\mathcal B_s$. Under the spectrum Hom bijection, a map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ acts on fibres by $f\mapsto f\circ\alpha$, where $\alpha:C\to B$. Commutation with the structure maps is exactly $k$-linearity of $\alpha$. The reconstruction lemma makes these Hom maps bijective and realizes every profinite continuous $G$-set by an ind-etale algebra, whose spectrum is qcqs weakly etale. Thus this explicit fibre functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective, giving the required equivalence $E$.

Apply the same construction with $k=\Omega=k^s$. Its automorphism group over itself is trivial, so the resulting equivalence is $E_{\bar s}:\mathcal B_{\bar s}\simeq\mathbf{Prof}$. For $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, base change is $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_kB)$; the split-fibre lemma identifies its fibre with $F_k(B)$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto a f(b)$. Naturality for every algebra map gives the asserted natural comparison with forgetting the action.

source.place: Example 4.1.10: separably closed case and geometric base change.

proof.text: For a family in $\mathcal B_s$, the covering test says that it is fpqc exactly when its geometric fibres have a finite jointly surjective subfamily. Every arrow between objects of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is weakly etale [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], so by the definition of the small pro-etale site these fpqc families are precisely its coverings. The same argument over $k^s$ gives the stated topology for $E_{\bar s}$. Any site object is covered by its affine open subschemes, each of which is qcqs by the affine-reduction lemma. This open covering is fpqc: on any affine target open, its intersections with the cover admit affine open refinements, and quasi-compactness selects finitely many. Every covering of a qcqs target has a finite covering subfamily by the covering test, so finite covering families generate the induced topology as in the qcqs-subsite definition. Hence the qcqs inclusion is cover dense with its induced topology.

source.place: Definition 4.1.1 and Example 4.1.10: covering families and affine-open density.

proof.text: In the tensor-fibre lemma take $L=k$ and $L=k^s$. The first embedding space is a singleton, so $E(s[P])=P$ with trivial action. The second is $G$, so $E(\bar s[P])=G\times P$ with left translation. Restriction along $k\subseteq k^s$ is $(h,p)\mapsto p$; a parameter map $v:P\to Q$ is $(h,p)\mapsto(h,v(p))$. These formulas give both natural identifications and the required structural-map normalization, including the empty parameter.
